This dataset contains 9 transects associated with the shoreline at site nzd0203 . Each transect represents a segment of the coastline for which elevation and positional data have been analysed to estimate shoreline change trends and related metrics.

The orientation of transects spans from 55.061 ° to 77.125 °, with a mean orientation of 66.289 °, indicating the general alignment of shoreline segments within this site.

Note: Orientation data is not available for this site.

In terms of shoreline change:

  • The average linear trend across all transects is -0.031 m/year, with individual values ranging from -0.243 to 0.208 , suggesting a net erosional trend overall.

  • The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the trend model averages 12.706 m, indicating the typical deviation between observed points and the fitted trend line.

Note: Trend analysis data is not available for this site. This may indicate insufficient temporal data for trend calculations.

Confidence intervals on shoreline position trends are also available:

  • The mean lower bound is 0.065 , and the mean upper bound is 0.086 , reflecting the uncertainty range around trend estimates.

The number of valid data points per transect ( n_points_nonan ) ranges from 546 to 582 , with an average of 565.111 .

Time Delimited Analysis

From January 01, 2000 to January 01, 2010

Data Processing

The analysis began with the complete satellite-derived shoreline dataset containing 695 temporal observations across 9 shore-normal transects. After applying the specified date range filter from January 01, 2000 to January 01, 2010 , the dataset was reduced to 183 observations.

These observations span 9.8 years, with an average of 147.8 data points per transect. The time-bounded analysis reveals an average shoreline change rate of 0.05 meters per year across all analysed transects. Individual transect trends ranged from -0.48 to 0.81 meters per year. The analysis processed a total of 1330 valid shoreline observations across all transects during the specified period.

The quality of the linear regression models is reflected in an average R² value of 0.01 , representing the proportion of variance in shoreline position explained by calculated trend.

Comparison

The original analysis, based on the complete temporal record, included 9 transects with an average trend of -0.03 meters per year (ranging from -0.24 to 0.21 meters per year). The time-bounded analysis shows 9 transects with an average trend of 0.05 meters per year (ranging from -0.48 to 0.81 meters per year). This represents a minimal change (0.020 m/year difference in magnitude) in average trend compared to the historical baseline. Model quality also differs between approaches: the time-bounded analysis achieved an average R² of 0.01 compared to 0.01 for the full dataset. This suggests the time-bounded period shows lower model reliability, indicating less consistent shoreline behavior during the specified timeframe.

Narrative Generation Configuration

Area of Interest Definitions

The area of interest (AOI) definitions are used to categorise shoreline segments based on their trends and characteristics. Each AOI has a priority, conditions for classification, and a description template for narrative generation. This report returns zones with, at minimum, 3 transects.

AOI Name Priority Conditions
No Data 1 If the `trend` of the intersect is null.
Rapid Erosion 2 If the `trend` of the intersect is less than -0.8.
Moderate Erosion 3 If the `trend` of the intersect is less than -0.3.
Rapid Accretion 4 If the `trend` of the intersect is greater than 0.8.
Moderate Accretion 5 If the `trend` of the intersect is greater than 0.3.
High Uncertainty 6 If the `r2_score` of the intersect is less than 0.05. If the `rmse` of the intersect is greater than 30.
Steep Beach 7 If the `beach_slope` of the intersect is greater than 0.08.
Low Energy 8 If the `beach_slope` of the intersect is less than 0.04.
Stable 9 –
